statement: For every undirected unit-edge-capacity graph with k indexed terminal pairs, one randomized algorithm runs in polynomial time with a polynomial bound on random bits, always returns a congestion-1 splittable unit routing of a subset of distinct original pairs, and with probability at least 3/4 selects at least OPT/[C log(k+2) exp(C sqrt(log log(k+4)))] pairs for an absolute constant C. Thus the full immutable source.md Conjecture 5.1 has a log^(1+o(1)) k approximation, with no congestion augmentation, fractional admission credit, restricted graph class, or n-for-k substitution. This is the proposer’s full-resolution claim pending fresh review.
contribution: A protected uniform-path-copy reduction composes one fixed integral-node-weight BJS2026 flow-expander decomposition with the prior corrected CKS congestion-1 matching rounding. Old unit terminal occurrence bridges prohibit duplicate-copy admission; a fixed-flow cut charge retains a constant fraction of copy paths; a small-k exact branch makes the remaining endpoint weight O(k^2). This avoids the unproved nonuniform rounding and changing-throughput interface and improves the current primary-source O(log^2 k) general-graph baseline to log^(1+o(1)) k. Uniformization, decomposition, and CKS clustering themselves are credited as prior work. The proposed nonroutine value is the full admission-preserving reduction and its original-target consequence; fresh novelty, significance and STOC-level assessment remain required.
